cells.tense: Right now, strength you have built up is finding its way to someone who needs it.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Decide which person or project this strength is for, and give toward it for a week without second-guessing the choice.
cells.core:
What you can do here is know what you've been developing and share the strength from it clearly, by measure. Nothing about that needs arranging or announcing — it moves because the work behind it is real, and the people receiving it can tell that apart from a gesture.

Next time you're deciding who gets what, hold the question for a minute first. Which light are you actually steering by? A direction you've chosen doesn't need defending once it's chosen; it needs you to keep handing toward it while the week runs. That's slower than answering whoever asks first, and the ones who receive from you will feel the difference over time.

cells.tense: Soon enough you'll be reading the scales on support that has not had a chance to land yet.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: Let your own sense of what's fair settle one small question of who gets what — nobody watching — and act before you check it with anyone.
cells.core:
When strength moves between people here, some part of you is already counting what's owed: who has had more, who has had less, what a fair share looks like before anyone has asked. Sharing gets heavier than it needs to be. What should flow has to pass a scale first.

Your own sense of what is right is still in there, and it can close a small case quietly. Give it one practice case you don't have to weigh: return what you owe, say the fair thing, and leave the tally alone. The count can wait until morning. What you hand over after checking fares worse for the checking, and people feel the calculation in it.
cells.sheetLine: You weigh what you give before it can leave your hands.

cells.tense: Strength meant to move between people is sitting still, and you are the one holding it.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Take the hard part you have been circling and sit with it once. Only that piece. Notice what holds while you're in it.
cells.core:
Where strength moves between people, it has gone quiet. You can see what's needed and you're not the one handing it over. This isn't stinginess — the impulse to give is still in you, aimed at nothing at the moment, and the room around it has gone flat.

What survives this isn't a decision; it's an old practice. Going back to the hard part for one sitting isn't a rescue and isn't a defeat. It shows you what's worth your strength, and what holds when you're inside it. Pick the practice back up for its own sake, not because someone needs saving. Support doesn't come back by deciding to care more; it comes back by doing one true thing.

cells.tense: Here, strength is leaving you steadily, and the hand steering it has not been claimed.
cells.act: decide the heading from what you want, not from logic
cells.ask: Choose one direction for your strength this week because you want it, not because the week needs it — then hold that choice without explaining it to anyone.
cells.core:
You keep people and projects upright, and from inside your story it just happens that way. The strength you share has a direction, but the one who chose it isn't claiming the choice. Whatever you were aiming for sits somewhere else in the account.

Try settling on the direction once: the place you're steering toward because you chose it, not because it's sensible. Then hold it without justifying it to anyone. Nobody else has to know, and you can drop it tomorrow if it doesn't fit. Sharing runs on knowing where you're pointed, and that knowing is yours — to keep or to put down. That's the part that's gone unspoken, and it's the only part.
